bottleneck: Dozens of neuroprotective drugs saved neurons in animal stroke models and failed in humans — a translational collapse so complete it discredited the entire field. The failures trace to treating too late (animals are dosed within minutes, humans arrive hours later), wrong patient selection, and animal models that do not replicate human stroke heterogeneity. The only proven acute therapies remain clot removal within hours, leaving most patients without options and the penumbra's dying neurons without protection. Billions in research produced a graveyard of failed trials and a generation of researchers who left the field.
current_state: Thrombectomy's success shifted focus to reperfusion; neuroprotection research is rebuilding with better trial design but has no approved drug after decades of attempts.

title: Stroke neuroprotection fails in translation
why_it_blocks: Stroke is a leading killer and disabler; the therapeutic window is hours and nothing protects neurons during it. The translational gap wastes decades of promising biology and leaves most patients with only rehabilitation.
